title: Net Billing Rider Terms — Share of the Bank Paid When the Customer Ends Net Energy Metering
content:
Under the Net Energy Metering riders valued at the avoided-cost export rates — Rider NBT-R Residential Net Billing Tariff, Rider NBT-C Commercial Net Billing Tariff and Rider NBT-L Large Customer Net Billing Tariff — only a share of the bank is paid when the customer ends the agreement while keeping service, and that share depends on enrollment in Demand Response Programs.

**Rule.** When the rider values exports at the avoided-cost export rates and the customer holds an active demand response enrollment, the paid share is the dispatch paid share of 0.95. When the rider values exports at the avoided-cost export rates and the customer holds no active demand response enrollment, it is the other paid share of 0.85. Under a retail-valued rider no reduced paid share applies.

**Records read.** The rider's valuation basis; the status of the customer's Demand Response Programs enrollments.

## Paid share

| Rider | Active Demand Response Programs enrollment | Paid share |
|---|---|---|
| Avoided-cost rider | Yes | 0.95 |
| Avoided-cost rider | No | 0.85 |
| Retail-valued rider (Rider NEM-L, Rider NEM-R) | Any | No reduced share |

## Hypothetical illustrations

- A Rider NBT-R customer enrolled and active in a battery dispatch program: 0.95.
- A Rider NBT-R customer whose enrollment is only enrolled and not yet active: 0.85.
- A Rider NEM-R Residential Net Energy Metering customer: no reduced share.
